history.summary: Shri Koteshwar Mahadev Temple stands at the foothills of Gwalior Fort, Sector-4 Shiv Sadan. According to local legend (unverified historically), the Shivling was originally installed in the Shiva temple atop Gwalior Fort; during Aurangzeb's 17th-century campaigns his soldiers dislodged it and threw it from the fort to the foothills, where it lay for about 150 years. The Scindia dynasty restored and reconsecrated the Shivling here as Koteshwar Mahadev in 1937-38. The temple is known for its ornate walls and ceilings depicting stories of Lord Shiva; just behind it stand an older Banjara Shiva temple and two stepwells connected to the temple's water flow. The Shivling is traditionally believed to be slightly tilted.

town_description: Gwalior is a historic city in northern Madhya Pradesh, dominated by the 8th-century Gwalior Fort perched on a sandstone plateau. It was the seat of the Tomar rulers and later the Scindia dynasty, and is celebrated as the birthplace of Tansen and the Gwalior gharana of classical music. Its monuments, including the Saas-Bahu and Teli ka Mandir temples, make it one of Madhya Pradesh's foremost heritage destinations.
